newsitem.title: USA: NHL - RED WINGS TRADE STANLEY CUP MVP MIKE VERNON TO SAN JOSE.
newsitem.headline: NHL - RED WINGS TRADE STANLEY CUP MVP MIKE VERNON TO SAN JOSE.

text.p: Veteran goaltender Mike Vernon, who backstopped the Detroit Red Wings to their first Stanley Cup championship since 1955 earlier this year, Monday was traded to the San Jose Sharks for two draft picks.

The Sharks had to part with only a 1998 third-round and 1999 second-round draft pick for the man who won the Conn Smythe Trophy as most valuable player of the playoffs for his contribution to ending Detroit's 42-year title drought.

"I can't lie, there is some bitterness there," said the 34-year-old Vernon, who turned in one stellar performance after another in compiling a 16-4 record with a 1.76 goals-against average in the Red Wings' championship run.
"All I heard was deliver the goods and I would get rewarded. That didn't happen in Detroit so I told them to send me to a place where I would get rewarded."

By winning the Stanley Cup, Vernon earned an automatic one-year contract extension. But he became the odd man out as the Red Wings decided to hold on to younger netminders Chris Osgood, 24, and 25-year-old Kevin Hodson.
"The decision to trade Mike Vernon was a very difficult one," said Red Wings general manager Ken Holland.

"Mike made some tremendous contributions to this team and had an outstanding playoff run, but with the NHL rules, we were forced to make a decision regarding our goaltending situation prior to the waiver draft and one of the three had to be traded," Holland said.
The Sharks did not disclose the terms of their contract with Vernon, but it was reported to be worth $8.25 million over three years.

"Simply put, Mike Vernon competes and is a winner," Sharks executive vice president and general manager Dean Lombardi said of the goalie who also backstopped the Calgary Flames to the 1989 Stanley Cup.
"He's a winner and that's great to instill in our young players," Lombardi said.
Vernon, who spent the 1996-97 regular season as backup to Osgood, was a surprise choice by Detroit coach Scotty Bowman to start in goal in the postseason.
Vernon had appeared in just 33 regular season games and went 13-11-8 with a 2.43 GAA.
In three seasons with Detroit, Vernon posted a 53-24-14 regular season record with a 2.40 GAA. He owns a 301-179-65 record and 3.13 GAA in 562 career NHL contests with Calgary, and Detroit.
